Story

En tant que mainteneur, je veux migrer DevDesk vers Bubble Tea v2, Bubbles v2, Lip Gloss v2 et ntcharts/v2 en une seule PR, en commits ordonnés, afin que l'arbre ne soit jamais mergé dans un état qui ne compile pas (la pile est couplée) et que la migration soit relue et vérifiée d'un bloc.

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given go.mod When la PR est prête Then il référence charm.land/bubbletea/v2 v2.1.1, charm.land/bubbles/v2 v2.2.1, charm.land/lipgloss/v2 v2.0.6, github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi v0.11.9 et github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2 v2.9.0, ne référence plus les anciens chemins github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss, ntcharts v1 ni muesli/termenv ; go mod tidy et go mod verify sont propres (Rule 303).
  • Given la PR When elle est ouverte Then c'est une seule PR vers main (aucune branche d'intégration charm-v2, aucune PR par lot), avec des commits ordonnés : (a) theme (color.Color, lipgloss v2), (b) testutil et touches, (c) routeur et architecture des vues, (d) API bubbles (textinput, spinner, table, viewport) et garde-fou KeyMap explicite des viewports qui reçoivent des touches, (e) ntcharts v2 et x/ansi, (f) profil couleur et suppression de termenv, (g) documentation (story DEVDESK-208). Les commits intermédiaires peuvent ne pas compiler seuls (pile couplée) ; la pointe compile et passe tout. La relecture se fait commit par commit ; le dépôt fusionne par squash, donc le message du commit final suit Rule 307.
  • Given l'architecture décidée (option C, choix de l'utilisateur) When le routeur est porté Then chaque vue de premier niveau garde Render() string et expose View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) } ; le routeur tient un map[ViewType]Screen, Screen étant tea.Model plus Render() string ; seul le routeur fixe l'état du terminal (AltScreen, couleurs, ReportFocus et autres champs de tea.View dans App.View) ; les composants (datatable, formulaires, FilterBar) gardent View() string ; la Rule 201 est conservée : les environ 480 signatures handle* renvoyant (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) ne changent pas.
  • Given les quatre ruptures silencieuses de la migration (espace, collage, ←/→ dans le viewport, largeurs) When la PR est préparée Then pour chacune un test existe ; pour (1), (2) et (4), il échoue sur le code v2 non corrigé avant d'être corrigé (le commit ou la description de la PR en apporte la preuve) ; le (3) est un test de non-régression et un garde-fou, qui ne peut pas échouer sur du code non corrigé puisque rien n'est cassé (le spike DEVDESK-198 a réfuté l'hypothèse, voir rapport §8) : (1) l'espace bascule une case à cocher et Entrée ne la bascule pas dans chaque formulaire ; (2) un collage atteint le champ focalisé (palette, formulaire, textinput, WrappedInput), y compris multiligne dans un champ d'une ligne, sans déclencher d'action ; (3) un viewport qui reçoit des touches (l'aide, help_overlay.go) ne défile pas avec ←/→/h/l, et une règle/test garantit que tout viewport recevant des touches fixe un KeyMap explicite sans Left/Right ; (4) un datatable rendu à trois largeurs occupe exactement l'intérieur du viewport et mesure de la même façon les cellules à largeur ambiguë (icônes Nerd Font, emoji, ZWJ).
  • Given la touche espace When la migration est faite Then \"space\" est centralisé dans keymap.Space (DEVDESK-200) et aucune case ne compare plus \" \" ; les tests des cases à cocher (Rule 135) et le test source de DEVDESK-200 passent.
  • Given les touches When elles sont portées Then tea.KeyMsg devient tea.KeyPressMsg, testutil.Key construit les messages par Code/Text/Mod et laisse v2 calculer String() (aucune table imposant \" \") ; les ctrl+c, ctrl+r, ctrl+p, q, ?, / ont le même effet ; TestOnlyThreeCtrlCombinationsSurvive et TestNoBareLetterIsNavigation passent.
  • Given un collage When il atteint la palette ctrl+p, l'aide, un formulaire, un textinput ou un WrappedInput Then le routeur envoie tea.PasteMsg au champ focalisé et le test de collage de DEVDESK-199 passe tel quel.
  • Given le profil de couleur When le programme démarre Then il est géré par Bubble Tea (ColorProfileMsg, tea.WithColorProfile ; forcé en TrueColor si WT_SESSION, à confirmer par le spike), le contournement COLORTERM de main.go est retiré, lipgloss.SetColorProfile disparaît des 13 fichiers de test (helper de DEVDESK-199), et TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString garde sa cause « thème figé ».
  • Given le nouveau moteur de rendu et la sortie synchronisée (mode 2026) When TestMeasureRedrawCost tourne Then ses chiffres sont comparés à la référence de DEVDESK-200 (consignée dans docs/backlog.md) et ne sont pas pires, ou l'écart est expliqué par écrit.
  • Given theme et datatable When ils sont portés Then Rule 119 tient (hex seulement dans colors.go), un thème utilisateur existant donne les mêmes couleurs, contrast.go lit les composantes par RGBA(), et un datatable (colonne d'icônes, ligne sélectionnée, ligne en erreur, Spans, Cut/TailStyle) rendu à trois largeurs occupe exactement l'intérieur du viewport (Rule 116 : RenderedWidth), sans séquence ANSI coupée (Rule 122), fond uniforme (Rule 115), colonne d'icônes de 2 cellules (Rule 125). Les golden tests de overlay et de datatable passent avec x/ansi 0.11.9 ; si la mesure runewidth diverge de celle du moteur, l'écart est noté pour une story de suivi.
  • Given main.go et setup/wizard.go When ils sont portés Then tea.WithAltScreen() disparaît au profit du champ AltScreen de la vue, m.AttachProgram(p) et p.Send depuis le MCP fonctionnent comme avant (Rule 110), les options de test (WithInput, WithOutput, WithoutSignalHandler, WithoutRenderer) des 3 tests sont adaptées, et les 4 sites tea.ExecProcess (shell conteneur, -it OCI, pager V, terminal ws) rendent le terminal à DevDesk sans artefact.
  • Given ntcharts/v2 When le sparkline du dashboard (internal/ui/dashboard/chart.go) est porté Then chart_test.go passe et le rendu est identique à seuil et taille égaux.
  • Given DEVDESK-145 (en cours, modifie internal/ui/security) When la PR atomique atteint internal/ui/security (30 fichiers, :sec) Then elle est rebasée après le merge de DEVDESK-145 avant de toucher ce package ; l'ordre « scan starting » avant le scan (tea.Sequence de inventory_commands.go) est conservé.
  • Given les portes de qualité When la PR est livrée Then mise run check et mise run test-race sont verts, golangci-lint a 0 avertissement (Rule 301, 305), les tests de S1 (DEVDESK-199 et DEVDESK-200) sont verts, et la PR est relue avec la skill dev-team:large-diff-review.
  • Given la vérification manuelle (DEVDESK-207) When la PR est prête à merger Then elle a été faite au minimum sur Windows Terminal (dk.exe) et WSL, matrice minimale décidée par l'utilisateur : les 4 ExecProcess, l'espace dans chaque formulaire, le collage et les couleurs.

Contexte

Effort : L. Priorité : Must. Dépendances (bloquée par) : DEVDESK-197 (Go ≥ 1.26.8, S0), DEVDESK-199 et DEVDESK-200 (garde-fous sur v1, S1), DEVDESK-198 (spike). Les relations Plane (blocked_by) ne sont pas disponibles sur cette instance (404) : dépendances posées ici, dans le texte. Bloque : DEVDESK-207, DEVDESK-208, DEVDESK-209, DEVDESK-210, DEVDESK-211, DEVDESK-212 et les stories F5 et F6. Entrée : .claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md (§1, §2, §4).

Décisions de l'utilisateur (2026-11-09) : migration ATOMIQUE en une seule PR, en remplacement des 6 lots sur une branche charm-v2 (stories DEVDESK-202 à 206 annulées, leur contenu est fusionné ici) ; architecture des vues : option C ; matrice de test minimale Windows Terminal + WSL ; pas d'usage SSH ni conteneur. Inclus : nouveau moteur de rendu et sync, profil couleur géré par Bubble Tea, routage de PasteMsg, \"space\" centralisé, viewport : garde-fou KeyMap explicite (←/→ déjà inactifs, voir spike DEVDESK-198), vigilance sur les largeurs. Ignorés : clavier Kitty / ctrl+shift, vrai curseur, souris, OSC 7501, nouveautés du viewport. Fonctionnalités reportées : stories de suivi du module.

Module : Migration Go 1.27 et Charm v2.

Spike DEVDESK-198 : hypothèse ←/→ des viewports réfutée, voir rapport §8.

docs/backlog.md:413:Until now the router ran one spinner chain (`jobTickMsg`) that broadcast a full `ChangedMsg` (snapshot and frame) to every held view at 10 Hz. The story asks for one tick that animates every row, blinking at 1 Hz, without rebroadcasting the snapshot. Decisions: (1) *One chain, renamed "animation"* (D2; formerly D5's "spinner chain"): `animationTickMsg{seq, at}`, `ensureTick`, `handleAnimationTick`, `animationState`. Only the router builds a `jobs.FrameMsg`; a source test enforces it. (2) *Two cadences:* 100 ms while `Running() > 0` (footer and row spinners need the frame), 500 ms when the view on screen implements `BlinkingView` and `WantsBlink()` is true and motion is blink. Otherwise no chain. (3) *The phase is read from the tick's own time:* `blinkOn = (UnixMilli/500) % 2 == 0`, so every row reads the same phase from the same tick. (4) *`FrameMsg{Frame, RenderedFrame, Blink}`* goes to the view on screen only, on every tick and on entry (`switchView`). `Frame` and `RenderedFrame` leave `jobs.ChangedMsg`, which keeps the snapshot only and now goes to every held view on a registry change. This reverses the earlier "one message and not two" comment, on purpose: the compiler then lists every reader of the frame, which protects against a view whose spinner freezes. (5) *Level signal:* `App.Update` is now a wrapper (`a.update` is today's switch, unchanged, then `ensureTick`). `ensureTick` runs after every message: it starts a chain when one is needed, replaces a slower chain by bumping `seq` (never two chains), and lets a live chain die at its next tick when nothing needs it. (6) *`tea.Every`, not `tea.Tick`:* `tea.Every` fires on the clock's boundaries, so `(UnixMilli/500) % 2` alternates strictly. With `tea.Tick` the drift accumulates and one blink is skipped (a steady 1 s `●`). (7) *Only the view on screen is asked `WantsBlink()`*, not every held view as the story's R3 said. Reason: the frame goes to the view on screen only, so a chain kept alive for an off-screen view would animate nothing. Stricter than the story; reversible in one line. (8) *`motionStatic` is a router field until A-02:* `setMotionStatic(bool)`, zero value = blink. A-02 wires it from `app.motion`; nothing is read from YAML here. `app.motion` does not exist yet (no `Motion` in `internal/config`). (9) *`datatable.Animating()` is not added here:* it has no caller before the first `BlinkingView` (A-09b/A-10a/A-13/A-14), and it goes with it. (10) *Four row-animation chains stay outside the router, declared as exceptions until A-16:* `oci_resources/busy.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-09b), `containers/update.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-14), `netdiag/ports_model.go` (`portsSpinnerCmd`, A-12), the OCI registry browser's `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (A-09a). A test lists them as declared exceptions: a new site fails it, and a stale exception fails it too. Criterion 4 of the story is therefore met on the router side here, and application-wide in A-16 (Q2, option A). (11) *Redraw-cost measurement is an in-process test, not a terminal capture* (Q1, option A): `TestMeasureRedrawCost` in `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`, skipped unless `DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`, runs a real `tea.Program` on the real router with `WithOutput(countingWriter)`, 120×40, for 10 s, and logs bytes per second for N = 0, 1, 20 blinking rows. The story named `TEA_TRACE`, which does not exist in Bubble Tea v1.3.10 (checked in the module source: no `TEA_TRACE`, no `os.Getenv`); the research document cited it from a page about another version. This measures what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows over SSH; the real-SSH check stays with the A-06 checkpoint, where H2 is consigned. No view blinks before A-06, so the PR cannot show "20 blinking rows" in the real application. (12) *No ADR:* a lasting decision recorded here, per the project's convention. Hand-off: A-02 calls `setMotionStatic`; A-06 adds `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` to `:jobs`; the first `BlinkingView` adds `datatable.Animating()`; A-16 absorbs the declared exceptions.

**Verdict : dans le seuil.** Les bytes/s sont identiques à la référence D114 (0 %, seuil +25 %) et redraws/s est égal à la cadence du tick (2 et 10).

## Contexte
- Commit HEAD : `56166bf8`, branche détachée (`HEAD`).
- `git status --short` : 35 entrées, dont 1 fichier suivi modifié (`docs/journal.md`) et 34 non suivis (plans `.claude/plans/*`, `docs/product/*`, `docs/ux/`). Aucun ne touche au code Go.
- Machine : Intel Core Ultra 7 155H (22 threads), Linux 6.12.94, go1.27.3 linux/amd64.
- Versions : bubbletea v2.1.1, bubbles v2.2.1, lipgloss v2.0.6.
- Protocole : 3 lancements séquentiels de la commande demandée, chacun d'environ 40 s. Tous PASS. Les sorties brutes sont dans `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-anthoni-projects-workspace-entire-anthnel-devdesk/3a0ae566-f2d0-46bd-8940-13efdfdce880/scratchpad/run1.txt`, `run2.txt` et `run3.txt`.

## Médianes sur 3 runs (terminal 120x40, fenêtre de 6 s)

| Cas | bytes/s | redraws/s | bytes/redraw | mean View() |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | n/a (0 appel) |
| blink-1 | 84 | 2.00 | 42 | 2092 µs (12 appels) |
| blink-20 | 1726 | 2.00 | 863 | 2015 µs (12 appels) |
| spinner-1 | 420 | 10.00 | 42 | 2021 µs (60 appels) |
| spinner-20 | 8629 | 10.00 | 863 | 1996 µs (60 appels) |

Pour bytes/s, bytes/redraw et redraws/s, les 3 runs sont quasi identiques (spinner-20 : 8630, 8629, 8629). Seul le mean View() varie d'un run à l'autre, de 1979 à 2248 µs.

## Écart avec la référence v2 de D114

| Cas | Référence D114 | Mesuré | Écart |
|---|---|---|---|
| blink-20 (bytes/s) | 1726 | 1726 | 0 % |
| spinner-20 (bytes/s) | 8629 | 8629 | 0 % |
| blink-20 (bytes/redraw) | 863 | 863 | 0 % |
| spinner-20 (bytes/redraw) | 863 | 863 | 0 % |
| blink-1 (bytes/s) | 84 | 84 | 0 % |
| spinner-1 (bytes/s) | 420 | 420 | 0 % |

## Critères du seuil D114
- **bytes/s :** écart de 0 % sur blink-20 et spinner-20, donc sous le +25 %.
- **redraws/s :** 2.00 pour blink et 10.00 pour spinner, soit exactement la cadence du tick, sans redraw en plus.

## Anomalies et remarques
- Aucune anomalie.
- Le mean View() est d'environ 2,0 ms. Cela correspond au « about 2.0 ms cold (v2) » de D114, qui précise que les 12 et 60 appels sont à froid, sans warm-up. Ce chiffre n'est donc pas comparable à l'isolated benchmark de 868 µs. D114 ne chiffre pas ce temps en v2 par cas, donc je n'ai pas calculé d'écart dessus.
- D114 donne la référence en v2 sur le même hôte, mais la machine actuelle n'est pas identifiée dans D114 (« the D110 host »). Les bytes sont déterministes, donc la comparaison tient. Le temps de View() ne peut pas être rapproché strictement.

M docs/backlog.md
 docs/backlog.md | 2 ++
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)
diff --git i/docs/backlog.md w/docs/backlog.md
index cbc141e3..ad2edf61 100644
--- i/docs/backlog.md
+++ w/docs/backlog.md
@@ -305,6 +305,8 @@ Bytes per redraw (20-row cases): 2905 Ascii, 5945 TrueColor, 863 v2. v2 repaints
 - **Harness defect fixed.** Without a TTY, v2 sends its own `WindowSizeMsg` built from a 0×0 size, which shrinks the router to a 489-byte view. The fix is `tea.WithWindowSize(...)` and `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` in `measureRedraws` (`e44dcb0`).
 - **Limits.** In-process, no TTY: this counts what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows. The v2 mode queries and synchronized output are not exercised; the real-SSH check stays with A-06. The `View()` study uses a dummy 120×40 view on one machine; real views are not profiled.

Voici les stories ouvertes (Backlog, sans parent) parmi les 100 work items les plus récents. Je n'ai pas lu les 259 plus anciens, donc la liste n'est pas exhaustive.

**Priorité haute**
- **Trace réseau (S-01 à S-07)** : DEVDESK-325 à 333. S-01 et S-02 sont des spikes de faisabilité (Linux natif, WSL2). S-03a (moteur `internal/nettrace`) et S-03b (onglet Path) viennent ensuite, puis S-04 (colonne de chemin), S-06 (Docker Desktop) et S-07 (WSL2).
- **Recherche d'images (IS-01 à IS-14)** : DEVDESK-299 à 308 (IS-01 à IS-04, IS-08, IS-09, IS-12, IS-13, IS-14, IS-03). IS-18 (DEVDESK-298), la fondation (erreurs typées, délai par registre), est à faire en premier.
- **CI / Dagger (spikes)** : S1 (343), S2 (344), S5 (346). S0 (342, `mise run ci`) est de priorité moyenne.

**Priorité moyenne**
- 341 : Footer, remplacer le spinner braille par la pastille d'activité partagée.
- 334, 335 : S-08 (plateformes non supportées, onglet grisé) et S-09 (jusqu'où l'appel va quand il échoue).
- 330, 331 : S-05a et S-05b (conteneur comme source, bridge vérifié sur l'hôte).
- 345 : S4 (test d'une Gate Dagger).
- 309 à 311 : IS-05 (tri), IS-06 (filtre), IS-07 (parcours du catalogue d'un hôte).
- Bugs : 297 (IS-15, détection de Docker Hub), 265 (Entrée sur `OptionConfirmModal`, contraire à la Rule 135).

**Priorité basse**
- 280, 281 : suivis Charm v2 (largeur des emoji VS16, coût de `View()` +27 %).
- 293, 294 : notification OSC 9 en fin de job, spike du curseur réel.
- 312, 313, 314, 318 : IS-17, IS-16 (bloqué, pas d'accès à un Nexus), exemple `agent_usage.prices`, ticks doublés (bug).

Lesquelles lancer ? Je te conseille 341 (petite, autonome) ou IS-18 (fondation de la série IS).

La PR #369 attend encore `Test`. Je la fais merger dès que c'est vert.

content.text:
Mène la feature suivante avec l'équipe d'agents : 341

Délègue chaque étape à l'agent indiqué (outil Agent) ; ne fais pas le travail toi-même.
Une étape peut être sautée si elle n'apporte rien : dis-le et pourquoi.

**Suivi** : si `341` est un identifiant Plane (ex. `DEVDESK-12`) et que les outils
`mcp__plane-orchestrator__*` sont disponibles, charge la skill
`plane-integration:plane-conventions` et suis la section « Suivi dans Plane » de l'agent
`team-core:orchestrator` : tu joues l'orchestrator, n'écris qu'avec
`mcp__plane-orchestrator__*` (tâches, assignations, états, comptes rendus), et transmets
l'identifiant au `reviewer`, au `tester` et à `devops`, qui commentent eux-mêmes.

**Avancement** : charge la skill `team-core:resume-work` et tiens à jour
`.agent-progress/<ID>.md` à chaque sous-étape, pour pouvoir reprendre avec `/resume` après
une coupure.

**Ne rien supposer** : un brief ambigu ou un choix qui appartient à l'utilisateur lui est
posé (`AskUserQuestion` pour un choix entre options). Quand un agent rend des **Questions
bloquantes**, pose-les à l'utilisateur sans y répondre à sa place, note les réponses dans
le fichier d'avancement, puis relance l'agent avec elles.

**Sobriété** : demande à chaque agent un compte rendu court (résultat, fichiers touchés,
points ouverts ; pas de journal de ce qu'il a lu). Les tests ciblés pendant les étapes ; la suite
complète une fois, à la fin. Un seul `coder` à la fois sauf
étapes réellement indépendantes.

1. **Cadrage** — lis la story : `workitem retrieve_by_identifier` (Plane) ou
   `gh issue view` (numéro d'issue GitHub). Si les critères d'acceptation manquent ou sont
   flous, `product-team:pm` les précise. Soumets les questions ouvertes à l'utilisateur
   avant de continuer.
2. **Conception** — `dev-team:architect` : plan en étapes livrables (sauf changement
   local et évident). Si `LLM_WIKI_PATHS` est défini (`printenv LLM_WIKI_PATHS`) et que la
   conception est structurante (nouveau composant, bibliothèque, sécurité, données),
   lance d'abord `dev-team:wiki-scout` avec le sujet et passe sa synthèse dans le brief
   de l'architecte. Fais valider le plan par l'utilisateur.
3. **Réalisation en TDD**, pour chaque étape du plan :
   - **rouge** — `dev-team:tester` écrit les tests de l'étape (critères, interfaces et
     comportements du plan) et montre qu'ils échouent pour la bonne raison. Étape sans
     test pertinent (config, infra, doc) : il le dit, passe directement au `coder` ;
   - **vert puis refactorisation** — `dev-team:coder` reçoit les fichiers de test et la
     commande, écrit le code minimal qui les fait passer, puis refactorise ;

{"result":{"id":"f68bc424-98a0-4de5-a760-0f74ec499039","assignees":[],"labels":["0d75b934-bc35-4b5d-9e3b-362237efc0a6"],"type_id":null,"created_at":"2026-11-11T10:09:38.795039Z","updated_at":"2026-11-11T10:09:38.879948Z","deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"Footer : remplacer le spinner braille par la pastille d'activité partagée","description_html":"

Story

En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk, je veux que le footer d'une vue qui charge des données (par exemple « Updating from GitLab... ») affiche la même pastille clignotante ●/○ que la colonne d'activité des tableaux, à la place du spinner braille, afin de lire un seul langage visuel pour « ça travaille », qui respecte le mouvement réduit et la perte de focus du terminal.

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given une vue dont le footer affichait un spinner braille pendant un chargement, When le chargement est en cours, Then le footer affiche la pastille ●/○ (couleur d'activité « en cours ») suivie du même texte qu'avant, et plus aucun glyphe braille.
  • Given plusieurs vues affichant une pastille de footer et des pastilles de colonne d'activité, When elles sont à l'écran en même temps, Then elles clignotent en phase, cadencées par le seul tick du routeur (500 ms), sans tick ni chaîne d'animation propre à une vue pour le footer.
  • Given app.motion: static, When un chargement est en cours, Then la pastille est fixe (●) et le texte du footer dit toujours ce qui se passe (« Loading... », « Updating from GitLab... »).
  • Given un chargement qui se termine, When il réussit ou échoue, Then la pastille disparaît, le message de succès (Info, temporisé) ou d'erreur (niveau Error, prioritaire sur le statut) s'affiche sans pastille, et la précédence erreur, avertissement, info, statut reste inchangée.
  • Given un chargement dont la progression est connue (par exemple « Scanning images 3/12 »), When le footer s'affiche, Then le compte reste dans le texte et la pastille ne suggère aucune progression.
  • Given un tableau en cours de chargement, When la vue s'affiche, Then le corps reste le tableau (en-tête, aucune ligne de remplacement) et l'état est dans le footer (Rule 128, Rule 139) ; le test TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody et la garde d'activité (activity_guard_test.go) restent verts et échouent si un spinner braille réapparaît dans le footer d'une vue migrée.
  • Given la livraison, When on relit les docs, Then Rule 128 (.claude/rules/tui-behavior.md), docs/architecture/app-shell.md (tableau « pastille de ligne ou spinner », cadence) et docs/architecture/ui-components.md (Status, indicator) décrivent la pastille de footer et ne mentionnent plus le spinner migré.

Questions ouvertes

À trancher par l'utilisateur à la prise de la story ; les critères ci-dessus valent quelle que soit la réponse.

  1. Périmètre : remplacer partout (15 sites Spinner: true, 10 vues), ou d'abord les 8 sites déjà pilotés par le routeur (jobs.FrameMsg) ?
  2. Progression déterminée : texte seul (« 3/12 »), ou aussi une barre ?
  3. Terminal sans focus : le ● figé suffit-il, ou faut-il ajouter « (paused) » au texte ?
  4. Garder la règle « pas de pastille quand le détail de la ligne sélectionnée a déjà un glyphe » ?
  5. À vérifier dans le code : les 7 spinner.Model propres aux vues (agentusage, containers, netdiag, explorer, oci, security, viewer) respectent-ils app.motion: static et le blur (DEVDESK-210) ? La réponse décide si leur migration est un correctif ou un confort.

Contexte

Effort : M — avis UX : docs/ux/footer-activity-indicator.md. Mesure citée dans la note : environ 376 B/s (tick routeur 1 Hz) contre 1 880 B/s (spinner 10 Hz). Sans module : ce n'est ni de la migration Go/Charm v2 ni un des epics « indicateur d'activité » existants (E1 à E3). L'effort M suppose le périmètre « 8 sites routeur » ; à réestimer par l'architect si la réponse à la question 1 est « partout » (probablement L, à redécouper).

À faire : (a) lis docs/architecture/app-shell.md et ui-components.md (sections animation, FooterMessage, indicator), components.FooterMessage et ses `Status`/`Spinner`; inventorie précisément les sites concernés (les 8 routeur vs les autres) ; (b) vérifie dans le code la Q5 : les 7 spinner.Model propres respectent-ils app.motion: static et le blur (DEVDESK-210) ? (réponse courte, pour une story de suivi) ; (c) produis un plan en étapes livrables et testables (TDD : interfaces, fichiers, tests à écrire, commande de tests ciblés par étape, ordre), en gardant Rules 110, 122, 128, 139 et les gardes existantes (activity_guard_test.go) ; (d) réestime l'effort.

  - L'étape 5 modifie la cadence du routeur : des tests sont à réécrire.
  - Aucun point irréversible : tout est interne, sans clé de configuration ni de thème.
  
  ## Effort réestimé
  **M** pour les étapes 1 à 6, **M+** avec l'étape 7. L'essentiel du temps passe dans la réécriture d'environ 30 assertions de test qui vérifient un `RenderedFrame` factice. Si l'effort doit être découpé : 341a = étapes 1–4, 341b = étape 5, 341c = étape 7 ou la story de suivi.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.

       entire graph capabilities --json

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). mise run run          # Build and run

mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package

mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |

| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client

- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

**Fichier** : `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-341-footer-activity-dot/internal/ui/forge/explorer/footer_loading_test.go` (non suivi par git).

**Commande** : `go test ./internal/ui/forge/explorer -count=1`. Elle sort `FAIL github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/forge/explorer 1.421s`, sans erreur de compilation. Sorties d'échec (tronquées) :
```
--- FAIL: TestLoadLinesCarryTheActivityDotNotTheOwnSpinner/{first_load,refresh}
    status Activity=false Spinner=true, want Activity only
--- FAIL: TestRefreshShowsTheDotBeforeTheUnchangedText
    want the dot before the text, got "... Updating from GitLab... "
--- FAIL: TestFirstLoadShowsTheDot
    want the dot before the load text, got "... Loading GitLab groups... "
--- FAIL: TestLoadDotFollowsTheBlinkPhase
    Blink=false must give the hollow dot, got "... Updating from GitLab... "
    Blink=true must give the filled dot, got "... Updating from GitLab... "
--- FAIL: TestWantsBlinkOnlyWhileLoading/{first_load,refreshing,idle}
    explorer.Model does not implement WantsBlink() bool (router BlinkingView)
--- FAIL: TestAnOwnSpinnerTickNoLongerReachesTheFooter
    a spinner.TickMsg re-armed a Cmd; the own tick chain must be deleted
    a spinner tick changed the footer: after = "⣽ Updating from GitLab..."
```

**Ce que couvrent les tests**
- `status()` pendant le chargement initial et le rafraîchissement doit renvoyer `Activity` et plus `Spinner`.
- Après `jobs.FrameMsg{Blink: true}`, le footer affiche `● Updating from GitLab...` et `● Loading GitLab groups...`, sans aucun braille.
- `Blink: false` donne `○`. Deux `Blink: true` d'affilée donnent un `●` fixe, ce qui reproduit `app.motion: static`.
- Explorer au repos : pas de pastille, `Activity` et `Spinner` à false.
- Une erreur l'emporte : `m.error` donne le texte nu, sans pastille. Ce test et celui du repos passent déjà aujourd'hui, ce sont des garde-fous.
- `WantsBlink()` vaut true au premier chargement et pendant `refreshing > 0`, false au repos.
- Un `spinner.TickMsg` ne renvoie plus de `Cmd` et ne change plus le footer.

**Tests existants à réécrire par le coder** (je n'y ai pas touché, et le plan n'en demande pas le marquage)
1. `frame_test.go` : `TestAFrameDoesNotOverwriteTheOwnFooterSpinner` est obsolète. Il pose `m.loading = true` puis `m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame("<OWN>")`, et vérifie que `<R1>` n'apparaît pas et que `<OWN>` reste. Il faut le réécrire :
   - `loading = true`, puis `FrameMsg{Blink: true, RenderedFrame: "<R1>"}` : le footer contient `●`, ni `<R1>` ni `<OWN>`, et aucun braille ;
   - `Blink: false` : le footer contient `○`.
2. `footer_activity_test.go` : `TestARouterFrameDoesNotReplaceTheExplorersOwnSpinnerFrame` pose `m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame("OWNFRAME")` et exige `OWNFRAME` dans le footer. Même réécriture : `●` ou `○` selon la phase, plus de frame propre. Le commentaire d'en-tête « migrate in step 7 » est à mettre à jour. `TestAFrameStillSetsTheBlinkPhaseAndStartsNoTimer` reste valable.
3. `footer_test.go` : `TestTheGlobalLoadKeepsItsSpinner` exige `st.Spinner`. Il doit exiger `st.Activity` et `!st.Spinner`, avec le même texte `Loading GitLab groups...`. `TestStatusDetailForAFailedDelete`, qui vérifie `● Deleting alpha/api · Updating from GitLab...`, est à revérifier : le `●` d'activité de la ligne de détail et la pastille de chargement ne doivent pas se doubler.
4. Tout test qui lit `m.spinner` ou `m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame` côté explorer (`index_test.go`, `api_test.go` l.215 en commentaire) est à passer en revue. Je n'ai pas vérifié ces fichiers un par un.

**Plane** : je n'ai pas d'outil plane-tester dans ma liste de fonctions. Je n'ai donc rien commenté sur DEVDESK-368 (43fff092-1d97-4b75-ab72-229be3e059a1), et ce compte rendu est à reporter.

**Hors périmètre** : je n'ai pas écrit le test `internal/app` « explorer refreshing, sans job : chaîne à 500 ms » du plan. Il relève de l'autre tester.
